4. MEASURES ADVANCED BY THE APPLICANT TO ENHANCE THE ENVIRONMENT OR TO AVOID OR MITIGATE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS
4.1 Preventative Measures and Monitoring
Page 4-2
The first sentence in paragraph four should be reworded to read: "The Section 4.1 has been revised. applicant is considering the necessity of augmenting stream flows in Howard Creek with discharges from Bad Creek Reservoir."
Page 4-4
Delete the second sentence in the last paragraph, since a surge chamber may not be necessary.
Section 4.1 has been revised.
Page 4-5
Only two exits from the powerhouse complex would be provided: the main access tunnel and the electric bus shaft. See Exhibit W, Subsection 1.6, Amendment 1.
Section 4.1 has been revised.
The last sentence in paragraph three refers to the leakage rate. This should be corrected to read: "ground water leakage rate",
No change required. The information in this paragraph is taken directly from Applicant's Exhibit W, page 1-9.
4.1.2 Recreation
Page 4-7
Existing natural areas include Coon Branch and Windy Falls only. Upper Laurel Fork Creek and Laurel Fork Creek Falls are not classified as natural areas.
Section 4.1.2 has been revised.
Quote: "the applicant would continue to refrain from harvesting timber within most of the trail corridor, "Crescent has consistently maintained it reserves timber management and harvesting rights throughout the general area, including the trail corridor.
4.2.1 Flora
Page 4-8
During summer 1974, individuals of the five rare plant species identified recommends that trail somewhat he by Dr. C. Leland Rodgers and Joseph E. Green, Jr. (Exhibit W, Appendix D) were transplanted to similar habitats outside the project area. In May 1975. observations showed the transplanted individuals to be thriving (see enclosure report #2). See Exhibit W, Subsection 2.2.3.1, Amendment 1.
Although Crescent reserves this right, the Applicant's letter dated January 25, 1975, indicated that "Cresent Land and Timber Corporation has been and will continue to refrain from havesting timber within most of the proposed trail corridor"
and adequate uncut buffer strips are being left along most of the trail corridor ... " by its recommends that trail segments be relocated if needs require.
Section 4.2.1 has been revised.
